nodes.content: Develop reinforcement learning transfer for robotic manipulation that reuses skills under hidden dynamics shifts while limiting negative transfer.
requirements: Match from-scratch success rates using 50% fewer target interactions when manipulation dynamics partially overlap.
On incompatible targets, stay within 5 percentage points of from-scratch success under equal interaction budgets.

nodes.content: Gate pretrained manipulation options by per-option probe-transition error, defaulting to a concurrently trained scratch policy above 0.15 normalized error.
What option-level compatibility signal and fallback should control reuse after observing target probe transitions?
A 0.15-error gate matches scratch success at half-budget on overlapping dynamics, with ≤5-point deficits at equal budgets on incompatible targets.
Fit option-conditioned predictors, collect 200 probes, and benchmark 0.15-gated reuse with scratch fallback versus scratch across overlapping and incompatible shifts.
Calibrate the 0.15-error gate on 200 probes per target, then compare gated and scratch success at 5,000/10,000 interactions.
ShiftGate-v1 benchmark logs probe errors, option choices, and success curves for gated versus scratch policies at 5,000/10,000 interactions.
Audit ShiftGate-v1 logs for gate calibration and success gaps: overlapping gated 5,000 versus scratch 10,000; incompatible equal-budget ≤5 points.
ShiftGate-v1 success: overlapping gated 5,000 interactions 64% versus scratch 10,000 78%; incompatible gated 10,000 61% versus scratch 70%.
Reject the fixed 0.15 gate and pursue uncertainty-calibrated reuse: overlap trails by 14 points; incompatible targets by 9.
Ablate option gating and concurrent scratch fallback on friction and gripper-lag shifts; measure false-accept rate and 10,000-interaction success.
On gripper-lag shifts, gating cut false accepts from 34% to 12%; scratch fallback raised 10,000-interaction success from 52% to 61%.
Can option-level gating retain reusable grasp skills while rejecting incompatible placement skills under a mixed dynamics shift?
Run 200-probe mixed-shift trials with unchanged grasp and altered placement compliance; compare uncertainty-calibrated option gating against all-or-none transfer.
Mixed shifts: calibrated gating reused 87% of grasp options, rejected 81% of incompatible placements; success was 73% versus 62% all-or-none.
MixedShift-200 packages probe traces, grasp/placement compatibility labels, and calibrated-gating versus all-or-none success curves.
Use uncertainty-calibrated grasp and placement gates with scratch fallback to reuse compatible options under mixed dynamics shifts.
Train uncertainty-calibrated option gates with scratch fallback; test held-out shifts against scratch at half and equal target-interaction budgets.
Using MixedShift-200, compare calibrated and fixed-0.15 gates with scratch fallback against scratch on held-out shifts at 5,000/10,000 interactions.
Held-out shifts: calibrated overlap success was 70%/5,000 interactions versus scratch 78%/10,000; incompatible success was 63% versus scratch 70% at 10,000.
Which failure mode explains the held-out 8-point overlap and 7-point incompatible deficits: miscalibrated gating or undertrained scratch fallback?
Gate miscalibration, not fallback starvation, drives both deficits; oracle compatibility labels will improve success by ≥5 points on each shift.
On held-out shifts, compare oracle compatibility gates with doubled scratch-policy updates at fixed 5,000/10,000-interaction budgets; measure success gains.
Oracle gates raised overlap success 70→77% and incompatible success 63→69%; doubled scratch updates added ≤1 point.
Prioritize gate calibration over scratch updates: oracle gates nearly closed both scratch gaps, while extra updates added ≤1 point.
Fit per-option conformal gates on MixedShift-200 compatibility labels, targeting ≤5% false accepts; audit held-out success with fallback unchanged.
Conformal probe-error gates targeting ≤5% false accepts replace fixed 0.15, achieving half-budget parity and ≤5-point incompatible deficits with scratch fallback.
Benchmark conformal gates against ShiftGate-v1 baselines on held-out shifts, checking ≤5% false accepts, half-budget parity, and ≤5-point incompatible deficits.
Conformal gates: 4% false accepts; overlapping success 78%/5,000 versus scratch 78%/10,000; incompatible 68% versus scratch 70% at 10,000.
Infer target dynamics from contact probes; reuse pretrained skills only when pessimistic value estimates exceed scratch-policy estimates.
Can 200 contact probes yield skill-value bounds reliable enough to reject harmful transfer without suppressing useful skills?
With 200 contact probes, pessimistic value gating yields ≤5% harmful transfers while retaining ≥80% of skills outperforming scratch.
Collect 200 contact probes per shift; compare pessimistic value gates with oracle skill returns for harmful-transfer rate and useful-skill retention.
With 200 probes, pessimistic value gating limited harmful transfers to 4% but retained only 61% of oracle-beneficial skills.
Using MixedShift-200 labels, measure 200-probe value-gate harmful-transfer rates and useful-skill retention separately for grasp and placement options.
On MixedShift-200, grasp/placement gates showed 3%/4% harmful transfers and retained 86%/82% of oracle-beneficial skills, respectively.
Which contact regimes cause useful-skill retention to fall from 82–86% on MixedShift-200 to 61% across all tested shifts?
Underrepresented intermittent-slip contacts (<10% of 200 probes) inflate pessimistic value uncertainty, lowering useful-skill retention below 65%.
Stratify probes by intermittent-slip frequency, then oversample slip contacts within 200 probes and reassess value-bound coverage and skill retention.
Reprobe the 61%-retention shifts and MixedShift-200 with slip-enriched 200-probe sets; compare retention and harmful-transfer rates against uniform probes.
SlipProbe-200 pairs uniform and slip-enriched contact traces with oracle skill returns and regime-stratified value-bound errors.
Stratify SlipProbe-200 by <10% versus ≥10% slip probes; compare value-bound widths and beneficial-skill retention before and after enrichment.
In SlipProbe-200, <10% slip probes yielded 0.24-wide value bounds and 59% retention; enrichment halved width and raised retention to 81%.
Adaptively allocate 200 contact probes to suspected slip regimes, then gate skill reuse using regime-calibrated pessimistic value bounds.
Implement adaptive 200-probe slip sampling and regime-calibrated value gating; test half-budget overlap parity and ≤5-point incompatible scratch gap.
Using SlipProbe-200 to calibrate value bounds, benchmark adaptive 200-probe gating against uniform probing and scratch at 5,000/10,000 interactions.
Adaptive gating reached 79% versus uniform probing’s 71% at 5,000 overlap interactions (scratch 78%/10,000); incompatible 69%/10,000 versus scratch 70%/10,000.
After confirming benchmark parity, test adaptive gating on 10-seed held-out peg-insertion and drawer-opening shifts against scratch at 5,000/10,000 interactions.
HoldoutManip-10 logs ten-seed peg-insertion and drawer-opening probe allocations, value gates, scratch baselines, and 5,000/10,000-interaction success rates.
Can adaptive probing identify rare slip regimes within 200 contacts without wasting probes on compatible targets?
Adaptive value-bound gates replace conformal gates, identifying ≥90% rare-slip regimes within 200 probes and limiting compatible-target slip probes to ≤30.
Audit HoldoutManip-10 probe traces for rare-slip detection by probe 200 and slip-probe counts on targets with compatible dynamics.
Replay conformal gates on ShiftGate-v1 and audit HoldoutManip-10 adaptive gates for scratch gaps, false accepts, slip detection, probe counts.
ShiftGate-v1: conformal overlap success 78%/5,000 matched scratch 78%/10,000; incompatible deficit 2 points. HoldoutManip-10: adaptive rare-slip detection 76%.
Calibrate adaptive probe-stopping on MixedShift-200, then audit HoldoutManip-10 for rare-slip detection and compatible-target slip-probe counts.
After MixedShift-200 stopping calibration, HoldoutManip-10 detected 76% of rare-slip shifts and spent 42 slip probes per compatible target.
Can conformal-gate uncertainty trigger targeted probes to raise rare-slip detection above 90% without exceeding 30 slip probes on compatible targets?
Conformal uncertainty-triggered probes detect ≥90% of rare-slip shifts within 200 probes while averaging ≤30 slip probes on compatible targets.
On HoldoutManip-10 shifts, test conformal-triggered probing against 76% rare-slip detection and 42 compatible-target slip probes, capped at 200 contacts.
On HoldoutManip-10, conformal-triggered probes detected 92% of rare-slip shifts within 200 contacts; compatible targets averaged 27 slip probes.
ConformalProbe-v1 records per-option uncertainty triggers, targeted contact traces, rare-slip labels, and compatible-target probe counts for HoldoutManip-10.
Adopt conformal-triggered probing over adaptive-only sampling: rare-slip detection rose 76→92%, compatible-target slip probes fell 42→27.
Gate grasp/placement options using conformal compatibility scores, trigger slip probes on uncertainty, and switch to scratch on rejection.
Does uncertainty-triggered probing preserve half-budget success and ≤5-point incompatible-target safety when probe contacts count toward target interactions?
Counting all probes, combined gating matches scratch's 10,000-interaction overlap success by 5,000 and stays within 5 points on incompatible targets.
Compare combined gating against scratch across overlapping and incompatible HoldoutManip-10 shifts, counting probes within 5,000/10,000-interaction budgets.
Integrate SlipProbe-200 calibration with ConformalProbe-v1 triggers; benchmark probe-inclusive overlapping/incompatible success against scratch on HoldoutManip-10 at 5,000/10,000 interactions.
ProbeInclusiveManip-v1 logs combined-gate and scratch success on HoldoutManip-10, counting probes within 5,000/10,000-interaction budgets.
Audit ProbeInclusiveManip-v1 for probe-inclusive overlap parity at 5,000 versus scratch 10,000 interactions and incompatible success gaps at 10,000.
ProbeInclusiveManip-v1: including probes, overlapping success reached 79%/5,000 versus scratch 78%/10,000; incompatible success reached 68% versus scratch 70%/10,000.
Using ProbeInclusiveManip-v1, rerun adaptive-only value gating on matched HoldoutManip-10 seeds; compare probe-inclusive success and rare-slip detection.
HoldoutManip-10: combined versus adaptive-only success was 79% versus 74% overlapping, 68% versus 65% incompatible; rare-slip detection 92% versus 76%.
Select combined gating over adaptive-only gating: probe-inclusive overlap parity, a 2-point incompatible deficit, and 92% rare-slip detection.
Using ProbeInclusiveManip-v1, validate selected combined gating on 10-seed payload and gripper-delay shifts against scratch at probe-inclusive 5,000/10,000 interactions.
PayloadDelay-10 contains ten-seed probe-inclusive success curves, compatibility decisions, and scratch baselines for held-out payload and gripper-delay shifts.
